chapters.summary: FDNY Chaplain Rev. Dr. V. Simpson Turner delivers an invocation on the eve of the 25th anniversary of September 11, honoring the 343 FDNY members, the 2,900+ lives lost, and those who died from 9/11-related illnesses in the years since.
chapters.title: Invocation by Rev. Dr. V. Simpson Turner honoring 9/11 first responders and victims

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: We will now have today's invocation, which will be delivered by the Reverend Dr.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: V.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Simpson Turner, the senior pastor of Mount Carmel Baptist Church, which is located at 714 Quincy Street in Brooklyn.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rev. Dr. V. Simpson Turner
utterances.text: Let us bow our heads.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rev. Dr. V. Simpson Turner
utterances.text: Eternal God, we come before you on this sacred eve.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rev. Dr. V. Simpson Turner
utterances.text: Standing in the shadow of a day, this city will never forget.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rev. Dr. V. Simpson Turner
utterances.text: 25 years have passed, yet the weight of that morning remains as real to us now as it was then.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rev. Dr. V. Simpson Turner
utterances.text: We remember the 343 members of the FDNY

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rev. Dr. V. Simpson Turner
utterances.text: who ran toward danger when every instinct in creation cried out to run away,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rev. Dr. V. Simpson Turner
utterances.text: who climbed when others descended, who gave the whole of their lives in the space of a single morning,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rev. Dr. V. Simpson Turner
utterances.text: whose names are etched not only in bronze, but in the hearts of this city.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rev. Dr. V. Simpson Turner
utterances.text: We remember the more than 2,900

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rev. Dr. V. Simpson Turner
utterances.text: souls taken that day, mothers and fathers, sons and daughters, neighbors and strangers who became family in grief.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rev. Dr. V. Simpson Turner
utterances.text: We hold their memory as sacred trust.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rev. Dr. V. Simpson Turner
utterances.text: And we remember, too, the hundreds who did not fall on September 11th, but in the years since, who breathed in the poison of those broken towers

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rev. Dr. V. Simpson Turner
utterances.text: as they searched, as they served, as they stayed.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rev. Dr. V. Simpson Turner
utterances.text: Their deaths came slower, but their sacrifice was no less complete.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rev. Dr. V. Simpson Turner
utterances.text: Lord, let this city never separate those names from the 343, nor from the more than 2,900.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rev. Dr. V. Simpson Turner
utterances.text: They are one line of the fallen.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rev. Dr. V. Simpson Turner
utterances.text: Written across 25 years instead of a single day.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rev. Dr. V. Simpson Turner
utterances.text: We ask for your comfort upon every family still carrying this loss, that they would feel even now that their loved one's sacrifice is not forgetting

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rev. Dr. V. Simpson Turner
utterances.text: forgotten by this city, this nation, or you.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rev. Dr. V. Simpson Turner
utterances.text: Grant courage to those who still serve in this city's firehouses, precincts, and rescue companies.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rev. Dr. V. Simpson Turner
utterances.text: Even those today who serve in city government, who carry forward the same willingness to do what's right, to run toward danger for the sake of a stranger.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rev. Dr. V. Simpson Turner
utterances.text: Grant us the living, the resolve to honor these lives, not only in remembrance, but how we care for one another still.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rev. Dr. V. Simpson Turner
utterances.text: May your peace rest, rule, and abide with each one of us.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rev. Dr. V. Simpson Turner
utterances.text: We ask this in your holy name.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rev. Dr. V. Simpson Turner
utterances.text: Amen.

chapters.summary: Shaun Abreu thanks Rev. Dr. Turner, congratulates Mount Carmel Baptist Church on its centennial anniversary, and highlights Turner's service as FDNY Senior Protestant Chaplain, his advocacy for the 12 Black firefighters lost on 9/11, and his work in housing and education. Abreu asks that the invocation be spread in full upon the record.
chapters.title: Majority Leader Abreu recognizes Rev. Dr. Turner's background and Mount Carmel Baptist Church centennial

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Thank you, Reverend Dr.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Turner, for today's invocation.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: I would also like to recognize Mount Carmel Baptist Church, which is celebrating a centennial anniversary.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Congratulations.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Reverend Dr.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Turner is a graduate of the Samuel D.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Witt Proctor School of Theology at Virginia Union University and the College of Staten Island.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: He was appointed by former Mayor Michael Bloomberg as Senior Protestant Chaplain of the New York City Fire Department and has also served as a chaplain with the Department of Correction and the New York City Sheriff's Department.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Reverend Dr.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Turner has lectured at colleges and international institutions, including at the United Nations, and has an extensive record of civic and community service.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: He has been a dedicated advocate for preserving the memory of the 12 black New York City firefighters who lost their lives on September 11, 2001, participating in annual commemorations honoring their service and sacrifice.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: As senior pastor of Mount Carmel Baptist Church and executive director of the Mount Carmel Brooklyn Housing Corporation, Reverend Dr.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Turner has dedicated many years to faith, public service, housing, education, and the Brooklyn community.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: We thank Reverend Dr.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Turner for his service, and I ask that his invocation be spread in full upon the record.

utterances.text: We will now have communication from Speaker Julie-Menin.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Okay, good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: I got to read the vote.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: My apologies, Madam Speaker.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Today's land use call-ups are adopted by a vote of 49 in the affirmative and zero in the negative.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Can I just ask everyone to take a seat?

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Just thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: So tomorrow, New York and the nation will, of course, commemorate 25 years since September 11, 2001.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: And tomorrow, we will honor the memories of the 2,977 people who were murdered that day.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: They were our first responders, our office workers, our fathers, mothers, sisters, and brothers.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: They were, in one word, our heroes.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: So I now am asking for a moment of silence in their honor.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Thank you.

chapters.summary: Menin discusses how the terrorists only made New Yorkers stronger, announces the Council's $1 million allocation for field trips to the 9/11 Memorial and Museum, and shares her personal experience serving on the jury that selected Michael Arad's memorial design.
chapters.title: Speaker Menin on 9/11 resilience and $1M for student field trips to 9/11 Memorial Museum

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: So though the terrorists not only killed those that died on 9-11, they tried to take away our freedoms and our way of life.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: They tried to proliferate fear.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: But quite frankly, they only made us stronger in our love for our city and our country.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: We will always remember the tremendous tragedy of that day, of the lives we lost, but we will also remember the extraordinary selflessness that we witnessed.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: From the thousands of first responders who rushed into the burning buildings to help people out of them, bridging the gap between human and hero,

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: to the ordinary New Yorkers who showed up as the sun went down, bringing food, drinks, handwritten notes to workers at Ground Zero.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Whether it's through the memories we pass down, their classes in school, or the field trips they take to the 9-11 Memorial Museum, it's imperative that our children who are not born on 9-11 learn about these stories.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: And that's why last week the council was so proud to announce that we

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: allocated a million dollars for field trips at the 9-11 Memorial and Museum to ensure that Never Forget is a promise our city's next generation will keep alive.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: I really want to thank all the members who joined.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: It was so moving.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: For a lot of the members who were there, they had said that they had never been to the 9-11 Memorial.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: They had never been to the museum.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: For me, this is something that is deeply personal.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: I served on the jury that selected the memorial.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: We went through 5,200 and design submissions from 63 countries to select Michael Arad's reflecting absence.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: And also, when you go into that museum, you get to hear stories from family members who lost loved ones, or you get to hear about the heroic acts of the first responders,

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: or literally the kindness of strangers who carried people down.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Flights and flights of smoke-filled stairs on that day.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: So really encourage any member that was not able to come with us to please go to the Memorial Museum.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: They would be happy to give you a tour, or I would encourage you to go with one of the schools in your district because we just funded these field trips.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: And certainly we do not forget history simply because a chapter is hidden from us or a chapter is particularly dark.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: If anything, that is the history we must always remember.

chapters.summary: Menin discusses her advocacy for the full release of the city's 9/11 environmental toxin reports, the commitment secured from Corporation Counsel Steve Banks, the new public portal launched this week, and $4 million in budget funding for the Department of Investigation to complete its report on the files.
chapters.title: Speaker Menin on release of city's 9/11 environmental toxin reports and $4M DOI funding

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: And so as someone who lost my own mother to a 9-11 related cancer, I have long advocated for a full release.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: of the city's 9-11 environmental toxin reports.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: During the advice and consent hearing of Corporation Council Steve Banks, we secured his commitment to release the 9-11 files.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: I also want to thank Councilmember Gail Brewer for her great work on this.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: She has been a champion.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: On the release of the files as well.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: So I was extremely pleased that this week the administration launched this new portal so that the public can finally view these records.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: New Yorkers deserve a full accounting of what the city knew

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: what might have been withheld from the public, and how their actions impacted first responders, downtown residents, and survivors.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: To that end, the Council also secured in the budget $4 million in funding for the Department of Investigation to complete and release its Council-mandated report on the files, another critical step towards transparency and accountability.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: The families of victims have questions.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: We do as well.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: And while the answers alone cannot bring back the lives we lost on that day, and look, I want to say over 9,000 people, more than

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: those died on 9-11, have now lost their lives to a 9-11-related cancer or illness, the city has an obligation to tell the whole truth, which is exactly what New Yorkers expect and deserve.

chapters.summary: Menin transitions to celebrate the first day of school for hundreds of thousands of NYC public school students, encouraging their growth and learning in the new academic year.
chapters.title: Speaker Menin marks first day of school for NYC public school students

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Okay, so to transition away from tomorrow's anniversary, today marks a new beginning for hundreds of thousands.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: thousands of public school students their first day of school.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Yeah, great.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Okay, that's sort of tepid applause, okay.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: I don't know why.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Let's give it up for our kids.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: This morning our young people dusted off their backpacks, swiped their student OmniCard, and reunited with their friends and their teachers after a long several months.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: The new academic year is another opportunity for them to learn, to ask questions, to be challenged, which is exactly how they will grow, and we are so excited for them.

chapters.summary: Menin notes tomorrow is the start of Rosh Hashanah and wishes Shana Tova to all Jewish New Yorkers observing the holiday.
chapters.title: Speaker Menin wishes Shana Tova for Rosh Hashanah

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Jewish New Yorkers, too, are celebrating in kind.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Tomorrow is the start of Rosh Hashanah, the Jewish New Year.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: I'll be attending synagogue with my family, reflecting on the past year, and I want to wish Shana Tova to all the Jewish New Yorkers who are observing.

chapters.summary: Menin recalls the first Labor Day in NYC in 1882 and her pride in joining labor's march, honoring the contributions of the American worker.
chapters.title: Speaker Menin reflects on Labor Day and workers' contributions

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Last Monday on Labor Day, we celebrated the incredible contributions of our workers.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: The first Labor Day actually took place in this city in 1882 when union members marched to Union Square to demand better working conditions.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: I was proud to join our friends in labor the other day on their march.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: We all benefit from their activism and continue to honor the steadfast American worker.

chapters.summary: Menin marks the start of Hispanic Heritage Month on September 15, celebrating the 2.5 million Latino residents of NYC and Latino council members, and notes Mexican, Chilean, and Belizean independence days in September.
chapters.title: Speaker Menin announces Hispanic Heritage Month and September independence days

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: September 15th marks the start of Hispanic Heritage Month, which 205 years ago on that day, Costa Rica, El Salvador, Guatemala, Honduras, and Nicaragua all gained their independence.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Throughout the

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: This month we celebrate the contributions and achievements of the 2.5 million Latino residents of our city.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: And we also recognize the pioneering Latino members of this body who serve our city as well.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Other Independence Days in September include Mexican Independence Day on the 15th, Chilean Independence Day on the 18th, and Belizean Independence Day on the 21st.

utterances.text: All good.

chapters.summary: Menin welcomes Minister for the Americas MP Chris Elmore visiting from the UK, and Allison Lee Turkell, Special Master for the 9/11 Victims Compensation Fund, who joined the meeting.
chapters.title: Speaker Menin welcomes special guests: MP Chris Elmore and 9/11 Victims Compensation Fund Special Master

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: We also had some special guests with us today.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Minister for the Americas, Member of Parliament Chris Elmore visited the Council from across the pond.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: And we are also honored, many of you joined for this, to be joined by the Special Master for the 9-11 Victims Compensation Fund, Allison Lee Turkell.

chapters.summary: Menin expresses deepest condolences to Council Member Darlene Mealy, whose mother passed away, and asks that her memory be a blessing.
chapters.title: Speaker Menin offers condolences to Council Member Mealy on mother's passing

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Lastly, on a more somber note, I want to offer my deepest condolences to Councilmember Darlene Mealy, whose mother sadly passed away.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: We are keeping her and her family in our thoughts, and may her memory be a blessing.

chapters.summary: Menin describes two land use items: the 47-03 108th Street rezoning in Thomas-Henry's district (119 units, 30 affordable, modified to R7D) and the 200 Kent Avenue rezoning in Restler's district (143 units, 36 affordable, modified to strike MIH Option 2).
chapters.title: Speaker Menin outlines land use items for vote: 47-03 108th Street and 200 Kent Avenue rezonings

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Now we're going to move on to our stated agenda.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: First, we'll vote on the following land use items.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: 47-03 108th Street rezoning will facilitate the development of a new mixed-use building with approximately 119

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: dwelling units, 30 of which will be permanently affordable under MIH Option 1, as well as retail and community facility space in Councilmember Shanel-Thomas-Henry's district.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: The Council has modified this application to rezone to an R7D district rather than an R7X.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: 200 Kent Avenue rezoning will facilitate the conversion and enlargement of an existing five-story commercial building into a mixed-use development with 143 housing units, 36 of which will be affordable under MIH in Councilmember Lincoln-Restler's district.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: The Council has modified this application to strike MIH option 2.

chapters.summary: Menin summarizes six resolutions up for vote: Resolution 7A (9/11 curriculum in schools), Resolution 6 (25th anniversary of 9/11), Resolution 82A (Feast of San Gennaro/Ferragosto), Resolution 429 (Alvin Ailey legacy), Resolution 402 (Carmen de la Valade Day), and Resolution 237A (Performing Artist Tax Parity Act).
chapters.title: Speaker Menin outlines resolutions for vote: 9/11 curriculum, 9/11 commemoration, San Gennaro, Alvin Ailey, Carmen de la Valade, Performing Artist Tax Parity

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Today, we're also going to vote on the following pieces of legislation.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Resolution 7A, sponsored by Councilmember Joann-Ariola, myself, and Councilmember Rita Joseph, will call upon the New York State Legislature to pass and the Governor to sign

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: legislation to incorporate a 9-11 curriculum in all New York schools.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Thank you to Katie Salina.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Resolution 6, sponsored by myself, would commemorate the 25th anniversary of the September 11th attacks.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Thank you to Regina Paul.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Resolution 82A, sponsored by Councilmember Amanda Farah-N.-Brooks-Powers, would celebrate the Feast of San Gennaro and Ferragosta Festival annually in September.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Thank you to Regina Paul.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Resolution 429, sponsored by Deputy Speaker Dr.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Nantasha Williams, would recognize the life and legacy of Alvin Ailey and honor his contributions to American dance and the founding of the Alvin Ailey American Dance Theater.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Thank you to Minora Boot.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Resolution 402, sponsored by...

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Deputy Speaker Dr.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Nantasha Williams would declare March 6th as Carmen de la Valade in New York City to celebrate her life and legacy and to honor her groundbreaking contributions to dance and theater.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Thank you to Regina Paul.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Resolution 237A, sponsored by Councilmember Crystal Hudson, would call on the United States Congress to pass the Performing Artist Tax Parity Act of 2025,

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: a bill which would increase the income limit and would make other modifications to the above-the-line tax deduction for business expenses of qualified performing artists.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Thank you to Regina Paul.

chapters.summary: Menin describes a pre-considered introduction co-naming 26 thoroughfares for 9/11, and Intro 906A sponsored by Justin Sanchez requiring DSNY to evaluate blocks with 7+ dog waste complaints per week.
chapters.title: Speaker Menin outlines pre-considered 9/11 co-naming bill and Intro 906A on dog waste complaints

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: A pre-considered introduction sponsored by myself, which would co-name 26 thoroughfares and public places with commemorative titles that honor the memory of the September 11th attacks.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Thank you to Brad Reed, Patrick Mulvihill, and Lucas Lopez Jensen.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Introduction.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: 906A, sponsored by Councilmember Justin Sanchez, would require DSNY, upon receiving seven or more complaints of dog waste on the same block within a week, to dispatch employees

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: to evaluate the block and enforce local health codes against animal waste in public spaces.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Thank you to Declan McPherson and Morgan Barrett.

chapters.summary: Menin describes Intro 813A by Harvey Epstein, allowing DCWP to refuse, suspend, or revoke tobacco or e-cigarette retail dealer licenses when the holder sells cannabis without proper state registration.
chapters.title: Speaker Menin outlines Intro 813A on tobacco/cannabis license revocation

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Introduction 813A, sponsored by Councilmember Harvey Epstein, would allow the Department of Consumer and Worker Protection to refuse to renew, suspend, or revoke a tobacco

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: retailer-dealer license or an electronic cigarette retail dealer license upon a finding that the holder of such license

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: distributed for sale any cannabis or cannabis product without the appropriate registration license or permit issued by New York State.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Thank you to the committee staff.

chapters.summary: Menin describes Intro 866A by Harvey Epstein, requiring DOT or permittees to post signs at the end of each block 48 hours before disruptive work begins, with details about the work and anticipated dates.
chapters.title: Speaker Menin outlines Intro 866A on disruptive work signage requirements

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Introduction 866A, also sponsored by Councilmember Harvey Epstein, would require DOT

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: or a DOT permittee, whichever is performing disruptive work, to post at least one sign at the end of each block where the disruptive work will occur at least 48 hours in advance of the start of said work.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Containing details as to who is performing the work and the anticipated start and end dates of the work.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Thank you to Elliot Heisler and Theo Miller.

chapters.summary: Menin describes Intro 804A by Phil Wong, establishing maximum allowable illuminance for residential outdoor lighting fixtures on one- and two-family homes in low-density residential districts.
chapters.title: Speaker Menin outlines Intro 804A on residential outdoor lighting illuminance limits

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Introduction 804A, sponsored by Councilmember Phil Wong, would establish a maximum allowable illuminance for residential outdoor lighting fixtures on one and two family homes in low-density residential districts.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Thank you to Sierra Townsend.

chapters.summary: Menin describes Intro 547B by Oswald Feliz, requiring DOHMH to designate warning symbols and statements for food items meeting or exceeding 100% daily value for added sugars, with public education outreach.
chapters.title: Speaker Menin outlines Intro 547B on added sugar warning labels

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Introduction 547B, sponsored by Councilmember Oswald-Feliz, would require the DOHMH to designate warning symbols and statements be displayed

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: next to listed food items that meet or exceed 100% of the daily value for added sugars.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: This bill would also require that DOHMH issue warnings for noncompliance, as well as conduct a public education outreach campaign to educate food establishments about the new requirements.

chapters.summary: Menin describes Intro 196C by Oswald Feliz, requiring DOHMH to develop rules for food service establishments to display warning symbols next to foods with 2,300+ milligrams of sodium per serving, with public education outreach.
chapters.title: Speaker Menin outlines Intro 196C on sodium warning requirements

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Introduction 196-C, also sponsored by Councilmember Fulez, would require DOHMH to develop rules requiring food service.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: establishments to display warning symbols next to foods that contain 2,300 milligrams of sodium or more per serving.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: This bill would also require that DOHMH issue warnings for noncompliance as well as conduct a public education and outreach campaign to educate food establishments about the new requirements.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Keeping us healthy.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Thank you to the staff, Christopher Pepe, Elizabeth Arts, and Joshua Newman.

chapters.summary: Menin describes Intro 220A by Kamillah Hanks, requiring DORIS to maintain a list of all known burial sites historically associated with formerly enslaved persons or African American communities citywide.
chapters.title: Speaker Menin outlines Intro 220A on African American burial sites documentation

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Introduction 220-A, sponsored by Majority Whip Kamillah-Hanks, would require

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: the Department of Records and Information Services in consultation with other city agencies to maintain a list of all known burial sites historically associated with formerly enslaved persons or historically African-American communities citywide.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Thank you to Declan McPherson and Alejandro Caraval.

chapters.summary: Menin announces three appointments the Council will vote on: Linda Garcia to the Land Bank, Dave Chokshi to the Board of Health, and John Mangin to the Board of Standards and Appeals.
chapters.title: Speaker Menin announces appointments for advice and consent vote

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: And then also we are going to be voting on the following appointments, which we have advice and consent over.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Linda Garcia to the Land Bank, Dave Chachke to the Board of Health, John Mangin to the Board of Standards and Appeals.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: So thank you for your attention.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: I'm now going to turn it back over to the Majority Leader.

chapters.summary: A council member discusses the co-naming of the intersection at West 33rd Street and 7th Avenue as Champions Plaza, celebrating the Knicks' unforgettable championship run and the New York spirit it embodied.
chapters.title: Council Member Wilson on co-naming Champions Plaza for Knicks championship

utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Speaker.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: We will now move into discussion of general orders, beginning first with Deputy Speaker Williams, followed by Wilson.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: I will proceed with Councilmember Wilson.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Councilmember Carr-Wilson.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN
utterances.text: Today we are voting on the co-naming of the intersection at West 33rd Street and 7th Avenue.

chapters.summary: Harvey Epstein discusses his two bills: Intro 866A, requiring advance signage for disruptive construction work to help disabled New Yorkers navigate, and Intro 813A, allowing revocation of tobacco licenses for illegal cannabis sales to support the legal market.
chapters.title: Council Member Epstein on Intro 866A (disruptive work signage) and Intro 813A (cannabis/tobacco license revocation)

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Councilmember Epstein, followed by Maloney.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: I'm honored to pass two pieces of legislation today, Intro 866 as well as Intro 813.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: 866 is a really simple thing.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: A lot of disability advocates and people in my community talk about crossing a street and getting through an intersection, and sometimes there's construction happening.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: We all see it.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: But it's very different for someone who's physically able versus someone who's disabled.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: And when you get to a corner and there's a construction, you can't go into the street, you can't get around it.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: It's been a struggle.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: And with the support of the community,

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: groups like Sydney and 504 Dems were able to pass this legislation that says, hey, city agency, you're doing work there, just put notices up, tell people, tell people who are in contact with their issues going on.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: It's a common sense piece of legislation.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: I want to thank the speaker and the staff who were able to get this done as well as my team on this legislation.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: The second bill is 813, and the speaker just mentioned that as well.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: And when I was in Albany, we worked hard on getting the MRTA to legalize cannabis

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: in this state and talk about why it mattered, to talk about the history of discrimination, talk about the history of black and brown New Yorkers going to jail and white New Yorkers not, and talking about what we needed to do to rectify that problem.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: And we entered into a process that allowed

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: people who are incarcerated or arrested for cannabis.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: Thanks, Carl.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: Good day.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: To get licenses and get those licenses first.

utterances.speaker: Oswald J. Feliz

chapters.summary: A council member explains voting no on John Mangin's nomination to chair the Board of Standards and Appeals, citing Mangin's role as an architect of ballot proposals that took land use authority from the Council, and arguing the BSA chair matters even more now that the BSA has greater authority.
chapters.title: Council Member Morano explains no vote on John Mangin BSA appointment

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN
utterances.text: Permission to explain my vote?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN
utterances.text: Permission granted.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN
utterances.text: Thank you, Majority Leader.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN
utterances.text: I'm voting no today on the nomination of John Mangin, and I want to explain why, because it is absolutely not personal.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN
utterances.text: John Mangin is a very smart guy.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN
utterances.text: He knows land use probably better than most people in this building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN
utterances.text: I met with him when he was here for his hearing, and I like him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN
utterances.text: I found him to be a genuinely nice guy.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN
utterances.text: If this were simply a question of intelligence or credentials, this would be a very different vote for me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN
utterances.text: But we're not hiring a professor of land use.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN
utterances.text: We're conforming the chair of the Board of Standards and Appeals.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN
utterances.text: And I keep coming back to what happened in this city and in this council just last year.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN
utterances.text: This council led an entire campaign urging New Yorkers to vote against ballot proposals that would take land use authority away from their elected council members and diminish the public's voice in the process.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN
utterances.text: We told New Yorkers that local input mattered.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN
utterances.text: We told them that these decisions shouldn't be moved farther away from the communities affected by them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN
utterances.text: I agreed with this council then, and I agree with it now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN
utterances.text: So I have a very difficult time understanding how we go from campaigning against those proposals

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN
utterances.text: one year to putting one of their principal architects in charge of the BSA the next.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN
utterances.text: Those ballot proposals passed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN
utterances.text: That's democracy.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN
utterances.text: I accept the result.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN
utterances.text: But precisely because the BSA now has greater authority, who sits in that chair matters even more.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN
utterances.text: The BSA is supposed to be an independent body.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN
utterances.text: It can grant variances, hear appeals, and make decisions that can fundamentally change what happens on someone's block.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN
utterances.text: And if you're the homeowner living on that block, where do you go?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN
utterances.text: You don't have a lobbyist.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN
utterances.text: You don't have a land use attorney on retainer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN
utterances.text: You may have taken a day off from work just to come down there and be heard.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN
utterances.text: I worry that we're creating a system where the public gets less of a say, the council gets less of a say, and then we put somebody who helped design that system in charge of one of the institutions receiving that power.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN
utterances.text: And that's a bridge too far for me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN
utterances.text: And that's why I'm voting aye on all with the exception of M88 and accompanying resolution 639 and M89 and accompanying resolution 640.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN
utterances.text: Gutierrez.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: I vote aye.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN
utterances.text: Thank you.

chapters.summary: Joann Ariola advocates for teaching the facts of September 11 in schools, emphasizing that children deserve to know who attacked the country, what happened, and who was murdered, without rewriting or sanitizing history.
chapters.title: Council Member Ariola on resolution for 9/11 curriculum in schools

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Councilmember Areola.

utterances.speaker: Joann Ariola
utterances.text: Thank you, Majority Leader.

utterances.speaker: Joann Ariola
utterances.text: Today we're taking an important step toward making sure future generations understand what happened on September 11, 2001.

utterances.speaker: Joann Ariola
utterances.text: But let me be clear, the facts of that day should never have needed a piece of legislation to force our schools to teach them.

utterances.speaker: Joann Ariola
utterances.text: 19 terrorists from al-Qaeda hijacked.

utterances.speaker: Joann Ariola
utterances.text: They deliberately attacked our country, murdered nearly 3,000 innocent people, and forever changed New York City and America.

utterances.speaker: Joann Ariola
utterances.text: Our children deserve to know those facts.

utterances.speaker: Joann Ariola
utterances.text: They deserve to know about the victims, the firefighters, the police officers, EMS workers, passengers, civilians, and ordinary New Yorkers who showed extraordinary courage that day.

utterances.speaker: Joann Ariola
utterances.text: And they deserve to learn the history without rewriting it, sanitizing it, or allowing politics to overshadow the truth.

utterances.speaker: Joann Ariola
utterances.text: We should teach the facts of September 11th, who attacked us, what happened, and who was murdered.

utterances.speaker: Joann Ariola
utterances.text: Today's vote is about making sure that history is not forgotten because we fail to teach the truth.

utterances.speaker: Joann Ariola
utterances.text: We risk allowing the future generations and forget why we will say never forget.

utterances.speaker: Joann Ariola
utterances.text: And thank you, Speaker Menon, for co-prime sponsoring this resolution and bringing it to the floor.

utterances.speaker: Joann Ariola
utterances.text: Thank you.

chapters.summary: A council member introduces Intro 1065 (DDC cost benchmarks for small capital projects), Intro 1064 (timeframes for agency approvals and change orders), and Intro 1063 (pedal-assist technology on pedicabs), citing concerns about capital projects going over budget and over time.
chapters.title: Council Member Wilson introduces bills on capital project cost benchmarks and pedicab pedal-assist

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: We will now move into general discussion.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: I'd like to let you all know we have about 20 folks signed up so far.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: So just keep that in mind.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: I'll start with Councilmember Wilson, followed by Maloney.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN
utterances.text: Thank you, Majority Leader.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN
utterances.text: Every year when the city allocates capital funding, I remain stunned at the price tags for these projects.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN
utterances.text: Too often, capital projects go massively over budget and over time for no clear reason and with little proper oversight.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN
utterances.text: Today I'm proposing legislation that aims to establish standards for the costs and timeframes for capital projects costing

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN
utterances.text: $10 million and under.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN
utterances.text: Intro 1065, alongside my colleague, Parks Committee Chair, Councilmember Hankerson, would require

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN
utterances.text: DDC to publish cost benchmarks for each type of small capital structure and to submit annual reports on the difference between those benchmarks and the actual cost of such projects.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN
utterances.text: Intro 1064, alongside Contracts Committee Chair, Councilmember Ressler, and again with Councilmember Hankerson,

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN
utterances.text: would require DDC to consult with the Mayor's Office of Contract Services and other relevant agencies to establish timeframes for completing agency approvals and change order requests.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN
utterances.text: I'm also introducing a bill that will set clear regulations regarding pedal assist technology on pedicabs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN
utterances.text: Intro 1063 allows pedicabs to be equipped with a basic electric motor that provides pedal assist when a pedicab is going under 15 miles per hour

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN
utterances.text: or a speed limit determined by the relevant agency and as part of a larger pedicab package that I look forward to working with my colleagues on to advance and work on those important pieces of legislation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN
utterances.text: Thank you.

chapters.summary: Virginia Maloney celebrates the co-naming of West 46th Street and 6th Avenue as Marsh McLennan September 11th Memorial Way, honoring 358 colleagues lost on 9/11, and introduces legislation requiring mental health providers to disclose when AI note-taking systems are used during patient care.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN
utterances.text: Councilmember Maloney, followed by Salam.

utterances.speaker: Virginia Maloney
utterances.text: Thank you, Majority Leader.

utterances.speaker: Virginia Maloney
utterances.text: First, I'm thrilled we passed a street naming at the intersection of West 46th Street and 6th Avenue, Marsh McClellan September 11th Memorial Way, in memory of the 358 Marsh

utterances.speaker: Virginia Maloney
utterances.text: McLennan colleagues whose lives were taken on September 11th.

utterances.speaker: Virginia Maloney
utterances.text: The co-naming gives those New Yorkers a permanent place in the landscape of the city they called home.

utterances.speaker: Virginia Maloney
utterances.text: Second, I'm introducing legislation requiring mental health providers to disclose when AI note-taking systems are being used during a patient's care.

utterances.speaker: Virginia Maloney
utterances.text: AI has enormous potential to improve health care, but patients deserve transparency about how and when it's being used and confidence that their most sensitive information remains private and anonymous.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN
utterances.text: Thank you, Councilmember.

chapters.summary: Yusef Salaam introduces Intro 1054 (requiring NYPD and DOC to fasten seatbelts for individuals in custody), Intro 1055 (Parks Department inspection and testing of public drinking fountains), and Intro 1056 (DOT parking permits for funeral homes).
chapters.title: Council Member Salaam introduces bills on seatbelts in custody, public fountain inspections, and funeral director parking permits

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN
utterances.text: Councilmember Salam, followed by Lewis.

utterances.speaker: Yusef Salaam
utterances.text: Thank you, Majority Leader, and thank you, Speaker.

utterances.speaker: Yusef Salaam
utterances.text: Today I'm introducing three bills.

utterances.speaker: Yusef Salaam
utterances.text: Intro 1054.

utterances.speaker: Yusef Salaam
utterances.text: Entry 1054 is about people in our custody.

utterances.speaker: Yusef Salaam
utterances.text: When someone is handcuffed in the back of a police car or a corrections van, they cannot brace themselves and they cannot buckle the seatbelt.

utterances.speaker: Yusef Salaam
utterances.text: A sudden stop can change their life forever.

utterances.speaker: Yusef Salaam
utterances.text: We saw that with Freddie Gray in Baltimore.

utterances.speaker: Yusef Salaam
utterances.text: I know what it meant, or means rather, to be in custody with your fate in someone else's hands.

utterances.speaker: Yusef Salaam
utterances.text: This bill requires the NYPD and DOC officers to fasten the seatbelts of individuals in their custody before transport, except in emergency situations.

utterances.speaker: Yusef Salaam
utterances.text: Custody should never mean surrendering your safety.

utterances.speaker: Yusef Salaam
utterances.text: Intro 1055 is about something as basic as a drink of water.

utterances.speaker: Yusef Salaam
utterances.text: On a hot summer day, children at a playground, seniors on a walk, and workers on their break all count on public drinking fountains.

utterances.speaker: Yusef Salaam
utterances.text: And it is our job to ensure that the water is safe to drink and aesthetically pleasing as well.

utterances.speaker: Yusef Salaam
utterances.text: This bill requires the Parks Department to inspect every public fountain and test its water at least twice a year, post signage showing whether the water is safe and when it was last tested.

utterances.speaker: Yusef Salaam
utterances.text: And maintain an online map that anyone can reach with a QR code.

utterances.speaker: Yusef Salaam
utterances.text: And lastly, Intro 1056 is about those who ensure our dignity even after we are gone.

utterances.speaker: Yusef Salaam
utterances.text: Funeral

utterances.speaker: Yusef Salaam
utterances.text: Directors take care of the bodies of our loved ones.

utterances.speaker: Yusef Salaam
utterances.text: They are an important pillar of our communities.

utterances.speaker: Yusef Salaam
utterances.text: Funeral directors should not have to choose between a parking ticket and a family's final goodbye.

utterances.speaker: Yusef Salaam
utterances.text: This bill lets funeral homes apply for an annual DOT permit so licensed funeral directors can park their hearses next to their establishments when posted signs prohibit parking.

utterances.speaker: Yusef Salaam
utterances.text: I urge my colleagues to sign on as co-sponsors.

utterances.speaker: Yusef Salaam
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN
utterances.text: Thank you, Councilmember.

chapters.summary: Farah Louis thanks colleagues for support after her father's passing, introduces Reso 626 urging the Senate to preserve protections for Haitian New Yorkers, Reso 624 designating October 17 as Wyclef Jean Day, and Reso 625 recognizing October as Reggaeton Heritage Month.
chapters.title: Council Member Lewis on Haitian immigration protections, Wyclef Jean Day, and Reggaeton Heritage Month

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN
utterances.text: Councilmember Farrah Lewis, followed by Shulman.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Thank you, Majority Leader.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: The sudden and unexpected passing of my father has left a profound void for my family and my community.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: I just wanted to take a moment to thank every colleague who called, text, attended home going services for my father, and sent flowers and kind words.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: I truly appreciate every gesture.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Today, I am proud to introduce three resolutions.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: For Haitian New Yorkers, unsound immigration policy has unfairly determined whether thousands of families can continue to work, provide for their loved ones, and remain safely rooted in the communities they call home.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: And what we are witnessing today is nothing short of cruel.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Haitians are being forced to wear ankle monitors, treated not as essential members of this city, but as criminals.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: We have seen the pain this inflicts firsthand in the story.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: of Pierre Damas and so many others that have been humiliated, destabilized, and living in fear.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: That is disparate treatment and injustice, and this body must say so clearly.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: At a time when Haiti continues to face devastating violence and displacement and humanitarian crisis, stripping these

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: protections puts our communities at risk.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Reso 626 will urge the Senate to pass S4814 to preserve these critical protections.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: I am also proud to introduce two resolutions celebrating the extraordinary cultural contributions of the Haitian and Afro-Caribbean diaspora.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Resolution 624 designates October 17th as Wyclef Jean Day,

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: honoring a Brooklyn-born Haitian, a Brooklyn-raised Haitian-born artistic artist whose music, philanthropy, and cultural pride have left an indelible mark in our city and world.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: And finally, Reso 625 would recognize October as Reggaeton Heritage Month, honoring a genre rooted in Afro-Caribbean and Latin American identity and recognizing New York City's pivotal role

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: in bringing vibrant Caribbean music traditions together.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: I urge my colleagues to join all these bills.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN
utterances.text: Thank you, Councilmember.

chapters.summary: Lynn Schulman introduces Intro 1060, requiring DOITT to create a dedicated 311 service request category for complaints about conditions in city jails, and publishing records of these requests to improve transparency and accountability.
chapters.title: Council Member Schulman introduces Intro 1060 on 311 jail complaint transparency

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN
utterances.text: Councilmember Lynn Shulman, followed by Marano.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: Thank you, Majority Leader.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: Today I am introducing Intro 1060, which takes

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: a common sense approach to making complaints about conditions in our city jails more transparent and easier to track.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: Currently, when an individual incarcerated in our city jails has a complaint about the conditions of their confinement, there is no clear or transparent way for that complaint to be tracked.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: These complaints can get lost within the Department of Corrections internal system, making it difficult to know whether an issue was addressed, improved, or if the complaint even reached the appropriate personnel.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: This legislation would require the Department of Information and Technology and Telecommunications to create a dedicated 311 service request category for complaints and service requests related to conditions within our city jails.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: It would also require the city to publish a record of these requests and update their status.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: Everyone deserves to be treated with dignity, and that includes people who are incarcerated.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: This legislation is about creating greater transparency and accountability so that we can ensure our city jails are humane and habitable.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: Thank you, and I want to thank the early sponsors on this, Tiffany Cabon.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: Selvena Brooks-Powers, Carmen De La Rosa, and I want to urge my colleagues to please sign on to this.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN
utterances.text: Thank you, Councilmember.

chapters.summary: Frank Morano introduces Intro 1051, providing property tax relief for NYC veterans with 100% service-connected disabilities, framing it as a recognition of service and sacrifice timed around the 9/11 anniversary.
chapters.title: Council Member Morano introduces Intro 1051 for veterans' property tax relief

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN
utterances.text: Councilmember Morano, followed by Palladino.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Thank you, Majority Leader.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: I've introduced a dozen very good pieces of legislation today that I hope you'll look at, or as my staff calls them, the dirty dozen, but some I think are worthy of your consideration.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: But I'm...

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Particularly proud to introduce Intro 1051, my bill to provide property tax relief for New York City veterans.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: We talk a lot in this chamber about affordability and about keeping New Yorkers in the communities they help build.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: And for veterans, particularly older veterans living on fixed incomes and disabled veterans, property taxes can be the difference between remaining in the home they worked a lifetime for and being priced out of it.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Our veterans did something extraordinary on behalf of the rest of us.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: They put on the uniform, accepted risks most Americans will never be asked to accept, and many came home carrying sacrifices that last a lifetime.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: And the timing of this introduction is especially meaningful.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Obviously, tomorrow marks 25 years since September 11th, and while we remember those we lost and the first responders who ran towards danger and the thousands of Americans who answered the call to military service in the years that followed,

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: remembrance has to mean more than what we say at ceremonies.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: It should also be reflected in what our government does, and that is what Intro 1051 is about.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: It's about making New York City a little bit more affordable for the men and women who defended this country and help veterans remain in the neighborhoods where they've put down roots if they have a 100%

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: service-connected disability.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: This isn't a giveaway.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: It's a recognition of service and sacrifice and of a debt that can never be fully repaid.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: I'm proud to introduce this bill.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: I hope my colleagues will join me in supporting it, and I look forward to getting it across the finish line very soon, hopefully by Veterans Day.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Thank you.
