utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN
utterances.text: Councilor Palladino, followed by Banks.

utterances.speaker: Vickie Paladino
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Vickie Paladino
utterances.text: I'd like today to introduce number 1057, 1052, a local law to amend the administrative code of the city of New York in relation to reporting data

utterances.speaker: Vickie Paladino
utterances.text: about micromobility device crashes.

utterances.speaker: Vickie Paladino
utterances.text: New Yorkers have a right to know where and how crashes are evolving.

utterances.speaker: Vickie Paladino
utterances.text: E-bikes, e-scooters, and other micromobility devices are occurring in our city every day.

utterances.speaker: Vickie Paladino
utterances.text: We cannot effectively address a public safety problem if we do not have the accurate and comprehensive information about it.

utterances.speaker: Vickie Paladino
utterances.text: This legislation will bring much-needed transparency and accountability to the micromobility crash reporting.

utterances.speaker: Vickie Paladino
utterances.text: It will require the NYPD and the DOT to collect and publicly report detailed information about crashes involving

utterances.speaker: Vickie Paladino
utterances.text: these devices, including injuries, fatalities, locations, times, and the specific type of class of that device that was involved.

utterances.speaker: Vickie Paladino
utterances.text: For years, our community has been in a state of crisis.

utterances.speaker: Vickie Paladino
utterances.text: have raised legitimate concerns about the dangers posed by reckless operation of e-bikes and scooters, particularly to pedestrians, seniors, and children, and people with disabilities.

utterances.speaker: Vickie Paladino
utterances.text: We need facts, not assumptions, to understand the scope of the problem and determine where enforcement and other safety measures are most urgently needed.

utterances.speaker: Vickie Paladino
utterances.text: Public safety must come first.

utterances.speaker: Vickie Paladino
utterances.text: If we are serious about making our streets safer, we need to know exactly what is happening on them.

utterances.speaker: Vickie Paladino
utterances.text: This bill is an important step towards greater transparency, accountability, and safety for every New Yorker.

utterances.speaker: Vickie Paladino
utterances.text: I would like you all to please sign on to this.

utterances.speaker: Vickie Paladino
utterances.text: Next, I want to introduce Resolution 636, calling upon New York State to...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN
utterances.text: I'll give you an extra five seconds, ten seconds.

utterances.speaker: Vickie Paladino
utterances.text: Ten seconds?

utterances.speaker: Vickie Paladino
utterances.text: I can't ever do anything in ten seconds.

utterances.speaker: Vickie Paladino
utterances.text: Look it up.

utterances.speaker: Vickie Paladino
utterances.text: It's about animal testing and how serious this is.

utterances.speaker: Vickie Paladino
utterances.text: It's, once again, intro 636.

utterances.speaker: Vickie Paladino
utterances.text: Don't take this lightly.

utterances.speaker: Vickie Paladino
utterances.text: Okay, take a look at that.

utterances.speaker: Vickie Paladino
utterances.text: How's that?

utterances.speaker: Vickie Paladino
utterances.text: Five seconds?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN
utterances.text: Thank you, Council Member.

utterances.speaker: Vickie Paladino
utterances.text: Oh, wait, one more thing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN
utterances.text: Sorry, Council Member, I have to move.

utterances.speaker: Vickie Paladino
utterances.text: Can I make a compliment?

utterances.speaker: Vickie Paladino
utterances.text: Last night, Linda Lee.

utterances.speaker: Vickie Paladino
utterances.text: I have to tell you, your dress was spectacular.

utterances.speaker: Vickie Paladino
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Vickie Paladino
utterances.text: Thank you, Council.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN
utterances.text: Councilmember.

chapters.summary: Chris Banks introduces Intro 1023 (allowing electronic property registration with HPD) and Intro 1024 (establishing a fair process for suspending or revoking press credentials with evidence at an OATH hearing), thanking property owners and the Speaker.
chapters.title: Council Member Banks introduces bills on HPD electronic registration and press credential due process

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN
utterances.text: Councilmember Banks, followed by Hanif.

utterances.speaker: Chris Banks
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr.

utterances.speaker: Chris Banks
utterances.text: Majority Leader.

utterances.speaker: Chris Banks
utterances.text: Today I'm proud to introduce bills, intros 1023 and intro 1024, that focuses on modernization, transparency, and accountability in city government.

utterances.speaker: Chris Banks
utterances.text: The first bill would allow property owners to register their properties with HPD electronically, including submitting required documents and electronic signatures and filing fees online.

utterances.speaker: Chris Banks
utterances.text: This legislation was developed in response to concerns raised by property owners and advocates about HPD's paper-based registration process.

utterances.speaker: Chris Banks
utterances.text: My office heard repeated complaints from the owners who submitted paperwork on time, only to be told later that it could not be located and had to be resubmitted, sometimes even when sent by certified mail.

utterances.speaker: Chris Banks
utterances.text: As one owner put it, HPD never loses the $13 in filing fees, but they always lose the paperwork.

utterances.speaker: Chris Banks
utterances.text: This bill creates a more efficient and reliable process by allowing registration to be completed online and reducing paperwork delays and the risk of lost submissions.

utterances.speaker: Chris Banks
utterances.text: I want to first of all thank Spony and small business property owners in New York for their participation and advocacy for this legislation.

utterances.speaker: Chris Banks
utterances.text: And also I want to thank Chair Perina Sanchez for allowing this bill to be passed.

utterances.speaker: Chris Banks
utterances.text: be heard in committee.

utterances.speaker: Chris Banks
utterances.text: I also want to thank the Speaker for her amazing leadership as well.

utterances.speaker: Chris Banks
utterances.text: I'm also introducing Intro 1024, which will establish a clear and fair process for suspending or revoking press credentials.

utterances.speaker: Chris Banks
utterances.text: Under this bill, the city would be required to show evidence at an oath hearing before a press credential can be suspended or revoked.

utterances.speaker: Chris Banks
utterances.text: This bill would allow also required the mayor's office of media and entertainment to review its current rules to determine whether updates are needed to make the process more transparent and consistent and fair.

utterances.speaker: Chris Banks
utterances.text: I urge all my colleagues to sign on.

utterances.speaker: Chris Banks
utterances.text: Thank you, Majority Leader.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN
utterances.text: Thank you, Councilmember.

chapters.summary: Shahana Hanif condemns anti-Muslim rhetoric from council members exploiting 9/11 to demand Mayor Mamdani not participate in tomorrow's commemoration, sharing her own experience as a Muslim New Yorker who mourned on 9/11 and faced years of surveillance and hate.
chapters.title: Council Member Hanif condemns anti-Muslim rhetoric targeting Mayor Mamdani

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN
utterances.text: Councilmember Hanif, followed by Gennaro.

utterances.speaker: Shahana K. Hanif
utterances.text: Thank you, Majority Leader.

utterances.speaker: Shahana K. Hanif
utterances.text: As we commemorate 25 years since the 9-11 terrorist attacks, we remember the thousands whose lives were taken and the families who have carried that loss for a quarter century.

utterances.speaker: Shahana K. Hanif
utterances.text: When we should be united in mourning, we are instead confronting a disgusting wave of anti-Muslim rhetoric from those exploiting this tragedy to advance a politics of hate and exclusion.

utterances.speaker: Shahana K. Hanif
utterances.text: Some here have demanded that Mayor Mamdani not participate in tomorrow's commemoration because he is Muslim.

utterances.speaker: Shahana K. Hanif
utterances.text: Mayor Mamdani has honored victims and survivors through action by finally releasing records they have fought decades to access.

utterances.speaker: Shahana K. Hanif
utterances.text: This will help responders and survivors get the care they need.

utterances.speaker: Shahana K. Hanif
utterances.text: care and compensation they deserve.

utterances.speaker: Shahana K. Hanif
utterances.text: On September 11, 2001, I was 10 years old, sitting in my fifth grade classroom at PS 230 in Kensington.

utterances.speaker: Shahana K. Hanif
utterances.text: Zohran was nine.

utterances.speaker: Shahana K. Hanif
utterances.text: Muslim New Yorkers mourned that day and lost loved ones.

utterances.speaker: Shahana K. Hanif
utterances.text: And then we endured years of suspicion, surveillance, profiling, and hate because of who we are.

utterances.speaker: Shahana K. Hanif
utterances.text: Acknowledging that harm does not diminish our grief for those murdered on September 11th.

utterances.speaker: Shahana K. Hanif
utterances.text: It is a part of our story.

utterances.speaker: Shahana K. Hanif
utterances.text: I'm asking my colleagues in this body to condemn the anti-Muslim hate coming from members of this council.

utterances.speaker: Shahana K. Hanif
utterances.text: Silence in the face of this rhetoric gives it permission to continue.

utterances.speaker: Shahana K. Hanif
utterances.text: Muslim New Yorkers belong here.

utterances.speaker: Shahana K. Hanif
utterances.text: New Yorkers of every faith and no faith belong here.

utterances.speaker: Shahana K. Hanif
utterances.text: Mayor Mamdani belongs at tomorrow's commemoration.

utterances.speaker: Shahana K. Hanif
utterances.text: Our differences can never determine whose grief matters, whose rights are protected, or who gets to belong in this city.

utterances.speaker: Shahana K. Hanif
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN
utterances.text: All right.

chapters.summary: James Gennaro introduces Resolution 622, calling on the state legislature to require municipalities to adopt an automated permitting platform for residential solar installations, citing NYC's rooftop solar potential and the Solar App Plus program.
chapters.title: Council Member Gennaro introduces Resolution 622 on automated solar permitting

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN
utterances.text: Councilmember Gennaro, followed by Dinowitz.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Majority Leader.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Today, I'm proud to introduce Resolution 622, calling upon the New York State Legislature to pass and the governor to sign S5781A6270, which would require

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: municipalities to adopt an automated permitting platform for residential solar.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: installations.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Currently, contractors are forced to navigate different paperwork and approval processes, adding unnecessary time and cost that ultimately gets passed down to the consumers.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: That is why the U.S.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Energy Department developed Solar App Plus, which was

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: specifically designed to address this problem.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: It provides a standardized automated process for reviewing eligible renewable solar projects while maintaining important safety and code requirements.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Many states have already adopted this app.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: And in New York City, city rooftops have the potential to house 10

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: gigawatts of solar generation at peak production.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: New York should remove needless barriers to residential solar, lower costs for homeowners, and make it easier for communities across the state to participate in our clean energy future.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: I hope you join me in supporting this important resolution.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN
utterances.text: Thank you, Councilmember.

chapters.summary: Eric Dinowitz introduces Resolution 620 (civic readiness seal for all NYC public high schools), Resolution 621 (arts and music curriculum in all NYC public high schools), and Resolution 619 (lowering the monetary threshold for design-build construction projects).
chapters.title: Council Member Dinowitz introduces resolutions on civic readiness seal, arts curriculum, and design-build threshold

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN
utterances.text: Councilmember Dinowitz, followed by Caban.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: Majority Leader.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: You know, there's a few things that...

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: can be more important than our children and the education of our children.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: But so often, the education of our children is measured on a very narrow scope of skills.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: And so there are two resolutions that I'm introducing.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: Resolution 620 calls upon the Department of Education to ensure that the seal of civic readiness is available to all New York City public high schools.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: This seal recognizes students who demonstrate civic knowledge, skills, and engagement, not just through coursework, but through service learning, research projects, and community engagement.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: This is the type of education that our students should be engaged in.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: Robust education that is more than just about a test and that engages the community.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: And ensuring that the seal is available at every public high school would give eligible students equal access to civic engagement.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: And next, Resolution 621, co-sponsored by Council Members Brewer and Thomas Henry, call upon the state legislature to pass Senate Bill 6318, requiring arts and music curriculum in all New York City public high schools.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: The arts are an essential part of a holistic education, and every student should have access to quality arts courses beyond art on a cart, which is what we hear about so many times in our schools.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: And arts in and of themselves have value.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: They are not just in service of advancing your English or your math skills.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: And finally, Resolution 6318.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: 619, veering off the education for a bit, calls upon the state legislature and governor to amend the New York City Public Works Investment Act to lower the monetary threshold for utilizing design-build in construction projects.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: This would allow for design-build construction.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: It's a process where a single vendor both designs and builds a project.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: It would allow for smaller city construction projects such as parks, prefabricated toilets.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: This would make projects more efficient and cheaper, and government efficiency is something we so desperately need in our city.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: Majority Leader.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN
utterances.text: Thank you.

chapters.summary: Tiffany Cabán associates with Hanif's remarks, thanks Schulman for Intro 1060 on jail complaints, and presents nearly 1,000 signatures from delivery workers supporting the Delivery Protection Act to improve safety and accountability for delivery workers.
chapters.title: Council Member Cabán on Rikers Island constituents, jail complaint bill, and Delivery Protection Act

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN
utterances.text: Council Member Kavan, followed by Epstein.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: First, I'd like to associate myself with the remarks of Councilmember Hanif.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: Secondly, I would like to say thank you for Councilmember Shulman's leadership on Intro 1060, of which I'm a co-sponsor.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: I represent the district that has Rikers Island in it.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: Every single person that is detained there is a constituent, and those are constituents that my office tries to help each and every day and is incredibly difficult in any system that makes it easier to be able to follow up with them, their loved ones,

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: and be able to speak with the administration and the agencies about rectifying those issues is incredibly important, so thank you.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: Third, I would like to just note that today I was presented alongside some of our council colleagues with this stack of almost a thousand signatures from delivery workers who, despite

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: wearing an Amazon vest are not Amazon employees.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: And it is all in favor and support of the Delivery Protection Act, which is ultimately a safety bill.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: It is one that will reduce crashes.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: It is one that will make sure that when employees get hurt, there is a recourse.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: It is one that will set safety standards across the industry and will stop big corporations from hiding behind false and exploitative subcontracting models to avoid the kind of

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: liability that they really should be taking on because they are acting as employees in that sitting.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: We're not alone in this.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: New Jersey's Attorney General has now filed suit against Amazon for exactly the same model.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: We have well over 30 co-sponsors on the bill, a host of support, not just from labor, but street safety groups and environmental justice groups.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: And so I urge my colleagues, if you're not on it yet, to please get on.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: It's going to make a huge difference to the livelihoods, the health and the safety of thousands of workers around the city.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: So thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN
utterances.text: Thank you, Councilmember.

chapters.summary: Harvey Epstein reflects on his personal 9/11 experience, the importance of combating Islamophobia, and highlights his youth council's eight years of advocacy for student transit access, including their recent report on the OmniCard.
chapters.title: Council Member Epstein reflects on 9/11, Islamophobia, and youth council transit advocacy

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN
utterances.text: Councilmember Epstein, followed by Hudson.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: I just want to welcome all the young people who went back to school today.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: I know it's a very exciting day, the first day of school.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: I remember every day walking my kids to school and what it really meant.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: Well, move a little closer to a somber topic.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: I know the Speaker flagged it earlier about 9-11 tomorrow, and I think we'll all be thinking about this tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: and thinking about it today.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: And I reflect on what that was like for me 25 years ago, thinking about, mentioned earlier, dropping my daughter at daycare and looking down First Avenue and seeing a plane hit the tower.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: And I was supposed to go to bankruptcy court that morning and I obviously couldn't go to bankruptcy court that morning because

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: There was nothing to do that morning.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: But trying to figure out what we could do and making sure my family was safe and everyone's family was safe and hearing about stories of friends and loved ones who got stuck and died and friends and loved ones who got out.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: And, you know, that story means so much to us and it means so much about the history and the fabric of New York.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: It means so much about what we need to be doing going forward, but also talks a lot about, you know, hate and Islamophobia and what happened after that in New York and how our Muslim brothers and sisters were treated in this city and in this country.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: So I hope when we reflect on that, we think about how we move forward.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: I also want to flag a more joyful topic, if I could, just around the youth council that I've had.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: And they've worked hard over the last eight years focusing on student access to public transportation.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: And in 2018, they really focused on the half-price MetroCard and getting rid of that card where people had to pay $1.35 and change, and then focusing on the full MetroCard and getting more swipes and announcing that.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: Mayor Adams in 2024 were some of our colleagues here.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: Just a few weeks ago, they released their new report where they interviewed over 700 students, talked about their problems with the existing OmniCard, released a report.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: And really, I encourage you all to look at the report and the recommendations to make that better.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: We want to inspire the next generation of young people to do more, and I'm proud that they did this.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: And I hope everyone has a lovely, happy new year tomorrow, La Santa Tova.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN
utterances.text: Thank you.

chapters.summary: Crystal Hudson delivers forceful remarks condemning Islamophobic and racist attacks directed at Mayor Mamdani, Council Members Hanif and Salaam, and Muslim New Yorkers, calling out colleagues who disguise prejudice as policy disagreement and demanding it stop.
chapters.title: Council Member Hudson condemns Islamophobic attacks on Mayor Mamdani and Muslim New Yorkers

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN
utterances.text: Councilmember Hudson, followed by Brewer.

utterances.speaker: Crystal Hudson
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Crystal Hudson
utterances.text: I generally do not engage with trolls and bigots, particularly online, but there are moments when silence is not an option.

utterances.speaker: Crystal Hudson
utterances.text: The repeated attacks directed at Mayor Zoran Mamdani, Councilmember Shahana Hanif, Councilmember Yusef-Salaam, and Muslim New Yorkers more broadly, which includes our own staff here at the council,

utterances.speaker: Crystal Hudson
utterances.text: demand to be called out for what they are, Islamophobic and racist.

utterances.speaker: Crystal Hudson
utterances.text: It is one thing to disagree with an elected official's policies.

utterances.speaker: Crystal Hudson
utterances.text: It is another to invoke the horrors of September 11th to smear a Muslim elected official who was nine years old when those attacks took place.

utterances.speaker: Crystal Hudson
utterances.text: To suggest that Mayor Mamdani or any Muslim New Yorker bears responsibility for the actions of extremists is not political disagreement.

utterances.speaker: Crystal Hudson
utterances.text: It is Islamophobia, it is racism, and it is dangerous.

utterances.speaker: Crystal Hudson
utterances.text: Our city knows the devastation of 9-11 too well to allow its memory to be weaponized against an entire faith.

utterances.speaker: Crystal Hudson
utterances.text: We lived through what weaponization looks like.

utterances.speaker: Crystal Hudson
utterances.text: Muslim, MENA, and South Asian New Yorkers

utterances.speaker: Crystal Hudson
utterances.text: surveilled, detained, and harassed in the years that followed, treated as suspects instead of as neighbors, simply for how they looked or prayed.

utterances.speaker: Crystal Hudson
utterances.text: The victims and survivors of that day deserve to be remembered with dignity, not used as a vehicle for hatred.

utterances.speaker: Crystal Hudson
utterances.text: My colleagues and their allies cannot continue to disguise their own prejudice as policy disagreement or political partisanship.

utterances.speaker: Crystal Hudson
utterances.text: You're not fooling anyone.

utterances.speaker: Crystal Hudson
utterances.text: In fact, you are hurting countless New Yorkers.

utterances.speaker: Crystal Hudson
utterances.text: Every New Yorker should be able to look at any member of this body, regardless of political persuasion, and see someone who respects them.

utterances.speaker: Crystal Hudson
utterances.text: Our disagreements as elected officials can be sharp, they can be political, they can be deeply felt, but there is a line between political disagreement

utterances.speaker: Crystal Hudson
utterances.text: and dehumanizing an entire community.

utterances.speaker: Crystal Hudson
utterances.text: That line has been crossed time and time again, and this needs to stop.

utterances.speaker: Crystal Hudson
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN
utterances.text: Thank you.

chapters.summary: Gale Brewer shares 9/11 memories from her district, introduces Intro 1025 limiting NYPD's police radio encryption delay to 15 minutes for journalists, and Intro 1026 allowing pedicabs to use taxi relief stands and establishing 15 pedicab relief stands.
chapters.title: Council Member Brewer on 9/11 memories, Intro 1025 on police radio access, and Intro 1026 on pedicab relief stands

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN
utterances.text: Councilmember Brewer, followed by Joanne.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Councilmember Hudson.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: A couple of things just to remember on 9-11.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: My predecessor, Helen Rosenthal's brother, was killed that day.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: And then to mention just this morning at a school, I learned that one of the parents has dementia, is not expected to live.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: She was at Trinity Church, and it is 100% based on 9-11 toxic.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: Never goes away.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: Intro 1025, I want to mention that earlier this year, local law 46, my law, went into effect.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: requires the NYPD to ensure that credentialed journalists retain access to police radio communications as the department moves to encryption.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: NYPD's proposed implementation would impose a one-hour delay, which is too long for journalists and photojournalists covering breaking news.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: So today I'm introducing this bill to limit that delay to no more than 15 minutes and require technology that allows journalists to scan multiple channels for active transmission

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: as they could with traditional police scanners.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: It is important to have timely access for journalists to report breaking news, to keep New Yorkers informed and provide independent oversight of this activity.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: I particularly want to thank Josh Kingsley of the council staff.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: He's a rock star.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: And all those from my office.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: Intro 1026.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: Last month, I introduced a package of pedicab reforms to improve safety, accountability, and regulation.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: This legislation today addresses another part of that work, how pedicabs use curb space.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: Now, drivers have very few legal places to wait for passengers or to take a break.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer

summary: The New York City Council held a stated meeting on September 10, 2026, presided over by Majority Leader Shaun Abreu and Speaker Julie Menin, covering land use items, legislation, resolutions, and appointments.

The meeting featured a solemn invocation by FDNY Chaplain Rev. Dr. V. Simpson Turner honoring the 25th anniversary of 9/11, and Speaker Menin's communication reflecting on the anniversary, the release of 9/11 environmental toxin reports, and the first day of school.

Council members introduced numerous bills and resolutions on topics including capital project oversight, veterans' property tax relief, micromobility safety, jail complaint transparency, and contracting reform, while also condemning anti-Muslim rhetoric directed at Mayor Mamdani and Muslim New Yorkers.
